title: Read your land: test your soil and choose where to start
course_title: Sustainable Agriculture Practices: Healthy Soil, Smart Water and Climate-Ready Farming

say: Read your land: test your soil, and choose where to start.
This is the video for Module 1 of Sustainable Agriculture Practices.
Sustainable farming keeps your land able to feed you next year, and when your children take over. Every bag of maize you carry away holds nutrients that came from your soil.

say: When stalks are burnt and nothing is returned, the soil gets poorer each season. Rain washes bare topsoil away, and the sun burns off organic matter, the dark crumbly remains that hold water.

say: Soil is alive. Rhizobia bacteria on the roots of cowpea, groundnut and soybean turn nitrogen from the air into plant food. Fungi help roots reach water.

say: The FAO describes three linked principles. First, minimum soil disturbance, so soil structure and soil life are not destroyed.

cards.d: Dig only where and when you must. Plant in rows or holes, and avoid burning before planting.
Keep the ground covered with crops, residues or mulch. Leave maize stalks on the surface.
Rotate crop families. Follow maize with cowpea or groundnut, or intercrop cassava with a legume.

say: Second, permanent soil cover for most of the year.

cards.d: Dig only where and when you must. Plant in rows or holes, and avoid burning before planting.
Keep the ground covered with crops, residues or mulch. Leave maize stalks on the surface.
Rotate crop families. Follow maize with cowpea or groundnut, or intercrop cassava with a legume.

say: Third, crop diversification. And sustainable does not mean no fertiliser. It means every bag works harder.

say: For example, Amina farms 1 hectare of maize near Zaria and burns the stalks every dry season. In year 1 she used 4 bags of NPK and harvested 40 bags. That is 10 bags of maize for each bag of fertiliser.
In year 4 she used 6 bags and harvested 36. Only 6 bags of maize per bag of fertiliser, a drop of 40 percent, with normal rain.
Two numbers written each year told the story. She will stop burning, keep stalks as mulch and bring in cowpea.
Soil is a mix of gritty sand, smooth silt and sticky clay. The mix decides how your soil holds water. Step one. Fill a clear, straight-sided jar about one third with soil.

panel.heading: The jar test
items: Fill a clear jar one third with soil
Add water to three quarters, plus soap
Shake hard for three minutes
Wait one or two days
Measure each layer with a ruler

say: Step two. Add water until it is three quarters full, and a few drops of dish soap to separate the particles.

say: Step three. Close it and shake hard for three minutes.

say: Step four. Leave it still. Sand settles in a minute, silt in a few hours, clay in one or two days.

say: Step five. Measure the layers. For example, Ifeoma in Nsukka got about 55 percent sand, 27 percent silt and 18 percent clay. That is a sandy loam: easy to work, but it dries quickly, so mulch and compost will help her most.

say: Push an open-ended tin about 5 cm into moist soil, pour in water 2.5 cm deep and time it. Use the second pour. Over an hour means the surface is sealed and rain will run off.

panel.heading: Water, structure, life and pH
items: Tin test: time 2.5 cm of water to soak in
Spade block: rounded crumbs, not plates
Count earthworms in the block
Most crops like pH 5.5 to 7.0

say: Dig a spade-sized block about 20 cm deep. Good soil crumbles into rounded crumbs. Poor soil comes out as hard plates or dust.

say: Count the earthworms. About ten or more is a sign of active soil life. Test three spots, top, middle and bottom of any slope.

say: Lime and wood ash reduce acidity, but too much locks up other nutrients. Apply lime only on a soil test's advice. Wear gloves and a dust mask when spreading it, and keep it away from children.

say: Now map your water, check NiMet's Seasonal Climate Prediction for your rain dates, and list the labour, materials and cash you really have.
For example, Hauwa grows maize and soybean near Kaduna. Rain runs off her crusted soil and dry spells hurt her maize. She scores each practice from 1 to 3 on cost, labour and impact.

panel.heading: Hauwa scores four practices
items: Residue mulch: 9 points
Tied ridges: 7 points
Composting: 5 points
Drip kit: 5 points

say: Residue mulch costs almost nothing and is easy, 9 points.

say: To remember. Put back what each harvest takes. Write down fertiliser and harvest every season. Test your soil at three spots. Get a lab test before liming. And start with one quick win.
